facts.statement: Saltoposuchus was a small, long-tailed crocodylomorph reptile belonging to the Sphenosuchia group.
facts.quote: Saltoposuchus is an extinct genus of small, long-tailed crocodylomorph reptile (Sphenosuchia), from the Norian (Late Triassic) of Europe.

facts.statement: The name Saltoposuchus translates to "leaping foot crocodile".
facts.quote: The name translated means "leaping foot crocodile".

facts.statement: Saltoposuchus possessed a long, pointed skull with sharp, flattened teeth adapted for a carnivorous diet.
facts.quote: Saltoposuchus has a long pointed skull and sharp, flattened teeth adapted for carnivory.

facts.statement: Paleontologists conclude that Saltoposuchus was a terrestrial animal based on fossil evidence.
facts.quote: Fossil evidence of Sphenosuchia and early crocodylomorphs lead paleontologists to conclude that Saltoposuchus is a terrestrial animal.

facts.statement: Saltoposuchus was likely a fast and nimble animal.
facts.quote: Saltoposuchus was likely fast and nimble.

facts.statement: The species Saltoposuchus connectens and Saltoposuchus longipes were named by Friedrich von Huene in 1921.
facts.quote: Saltoposuchus connectens and Saltoposuchus longipes were discovered and named by German paleontologist Friedrich von Huene in 1921.

facts.statement: Fossils were found in the Burrer Quarry in the Löwenstein Formation of south-west Germany.
facts.quote: Both species were found in the Burrer Quarry, Pfaffenhofen, which is an Alaunian terrestrial sandstone/marl in the Löwenstein Formation of south-west Germany.

facts.statement: Saltoposuchus lived during the Late Triassic Period, approximately 215.6 to 212.0 million years ago.
facts.quote: The Löwenstein Formation has been dated back to 215.6 - 212.0 Ma, which dates back to the Late Triassic Period.

facts.statement: Saltoposuchus existed in Europe, specifically within the supercontinent Laurasia.
facts.quote: Fossils found in Germany indicate that Saltoposuchus existed in Europe, or more appropriately, Laurasia.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Terrestrisuchus is a juvenile synonym of Saltoposuchus, as anatomical differences have been identified despite similarities.
facts.quote: It has been proposed that Terrestrisuchus was a juvenile junior synonym of Saltoposuchus, due to the similar anatomy and comparatively larger and more robust constitution of the latter, but several apparent anatomical differences between the two have been identified.

facts.statement: Saltoposuchus was a quadrupedal terrestrial reptile of small size, approximately 1 meter long.
